ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Financial Sanctions List, Taiwan Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau money laundering offenders list, and PRC sanctions and red-flag lists; PEP status must be expressly declared, verified against open-source intelligence and commercial databases, and re-run at least every 180 days until incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Online Company Name Pre-Approval System (公司名稱及所營事業預查系統) via GCIS portal (https://gcis.nat.gov.tw/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory name must be in Traditional Chinese characters; Simplified Chinese characters are not accepted for official registration. An English name may be registered as a supplementary legal name only after incorporation, and the Chinese name remains the controlling statutory name. Transliteration of the PRC parent's name must be based on standard Traditional Chinese character mapping and must not create phonetic conflicts with existing registered companies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name pre-approval is rejected, the applicant may file one administrative reconsideration petition with the MOEA Department of Commercial Administration within 30 days of the rejection notice, stating the basis of non-conflict and distinctive character. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may initiate administrative litigation before the Taipei High Administrative Court. Alternatively, the applicant may simply reserve a new name through the same online portal without waiting for the appeal route.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for industrial quick-freezing food manufacturing. A registered office address is mandatory and must be a physical address in Taiwan; a P.O. box or mail-forwarding virtual office is not sufficient. A business-management office address may be accepted only for the administrative representative office before the factory is established, but the factory license application requires a dedicated physical frozen-food processing premises subject to municipal zoning and food-safety inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 95% probability of a mandatory pre-operating on-site inspection by the Municipal Health Bureau and Industrial Development Bureau before Food Safety and Hygiene Management Act license issuance; 75% annual probability of unannounced follow-up inspections for frozen dim sum manufacturing facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局); online service portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (电子税务局) accessible via provincial STI domains; export-tax administration sub-portal: Export Tax Rebate System (出口退税管理系统); customs interface: China International Trade Single Window (中国国际贸易单一窗口).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investor incorporates the WFOE at SAMR (State Administration for Market Regulation) and automatically receives the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (统一社会信用代码), which serves as the statutory TIN; tax registration is completed online via the Electronic Tax Bureau within 30 days of incorporation, with supplementary filings for bank deposit account numbers, accounting software details, and VAT general taxpayer status election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise (居民企业) taxed on worldwide income at 25% CIT; VAT status defaults to general taxpayer (一般纳税人) for manufacturing exporters; no pass-through or flow-through tax treatment is recognized under PRC law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Elections available: (1) voluntary VAT general taxpayer election before the mandatory RMB 5 million annual sales threshold; (2) simplified VAT small-scale taxpayer election at 3% for limited domestic turnover, although export rebate qualification requires general taxpayer status; (3) CIT prepayment base elections (actual/prior-year/estimated); (4) annual election for the small low-profit enterprise preferential regime subject to statutory thresholds; no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections exist; anti-hybridity is enforced via CIT Art. 46 thin-capitalization rules and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.cross_strait_note: Taiwan is treated as a separate customs territory under PRC export-tax practice; goods shipped from the mainland WFOE to Taiwan qualify as exports for VAT zero-rating and are governed by the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement for income-tax relief; the WFOE must maintain a Taiwan buyer contract and cross-strait settlement records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_compliance: All elections are filed through the Electronic Tax Bureau with mandatory supporting schedules; late filing of election status changes triggers a CNY 2,000–10,000 compliance penalty per the Tax Collection Law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_authority_prefiling_interaction: Tax registration is auto-populated from the SAMR business license registry; a tax deposit account registration and an e-invoice quota application must be completed before the first export invoice issuance; post-registration field inspection by the local STI bureau may be scheduled within 90 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.record_keeping_mandate: Books and records must be retained in Chinese with supporting vouchers for at least 10 years under PRC accounting and tax laws; digital invoices must be archived in the national e-invoice database with real-time access for tax auditors.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.certificate_of_residence_procedure: The WFOE may apply for a PRC tax residence certificate (中国税收居民身份证明) via the Electronic Tax Bureau when treaty/cross-strait relief is claimed; processing time is 10 working days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.filing_calendar_summary: CIT annual return by May 31; CIT quarterly prepayments by April 15/July 15/October 15/January 15; VAT monthly/quarterly returns by the 15th of the following period; export tax rebate declaration within the following tax declaration period from the export customs date.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_administration_golden_tax_alignment: The WFOE is enrolled in the Golden Tax Phase IV (金税四期) system with real-time invoice, customs, and bank settlement data matching; anomalies trigger automatic audit alerts.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No incorporation-based threshold: VAT registration is mandatory for all WFOEs from legal establishment; the small-scale taxpayer simplified regime applies only when annual taxable sales ≤ RMB 5,000,000, but export zero-rating and the 免抵退 (exemption-credit-refund) method are exclusively available to VAT general taxpayers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory fully digital special VAT invoices (数电票) under Golden Tax Phase IV; issuance exclusively through the Electronic Tax Bureau invoice service platform with real-time XML/API clearance and unique encryption verification codes; traditional physical stamping abolished; export transactions require the export electronic invoice, customs e-declaration, and electronic manifest data; food exports additionally require GACC inspection release and e-quarantine certificates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.vat_data_matching_nexus: The electronic invoice platform automatically reconciles invoice amounts against the export customs declaration and the export rebate declaration system; any mismatch exceeding 1% triggers an audit hold and requires manual submission of proof documentation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.vat_input_credit_recovery: Input VAT on direct production materials, packaging, energy, and logistics is available for rebate under the 免抵退 method; input VAT on non-deductible items (employee welfare, motor vehicles for personal use, entertainment) must be reversed at 13%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.vat_zero_rated_supply_register: The WFOE must register the exact HR/HS commodity code (e.g., HS 1902.30 for frozen dumplings) and the corresponding export rebate rate; failure to declare accurate HTS classification creates a rebate differential subject to interest.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.turnover_tax_for_exports_to_taiwan: Goods exported to Taiwan are not subject to mainland VAT output tax; a zero-rated invoice is issued and the rebate filing references the customs e-export declaration; the sale is reported as export turnover in the VAT return.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.digital_reporting_frequency: VAT returns and electronic invoice summaries are filed monthly; export rebate declarations are filed monthly or quarterly at the taxpayer's election with a cap of 12 filing periods per calendar year.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.post_clearance_intervention: The General Administration of Customs (GACC) applies risk-based post-clearance audits on frozen food export declarations, including origin verification, cold-chain regulatory compliance, and export price reasonableness; adverse findings stop the rebate process.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A production-enterprise WFOE is eligible for the export tax zero-rating and refund (免抵退) regime when: (1) the goods are self-produced frozen dim sum physically exported from mainland China to Taiwan via a seaport/airport; (2) the enterprise holds VAT general taxpayer status; (3) the export customs declaration, bill of lading, and foreign exchange receipt are all completed and internally consistent; (4) the rebate declaration is filed within the statutory window (no later than the following year's April 30 tax filing period); (5) export proceeds are received and verified via a bank settlement slip within 180 days of export customs clearance. Taiwan is recognized as a separate customs territory, so exports to Taiwan are treated as export transactions eligible for the zero VAT rate and full input VAT refund at the statutory export rebate rate (13% for HS 1902/1904/1905 pre-cooked frozen products; the enterprise must verify product-specific rebate codes in the current-year rebate rate schedule; reduced rebate months may apply to certain processed food codes requiring the 10% refund differential classified as a cost).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) with GACC net-clearance and bonded/port status code
Bill of Lading or combined transport waybill (提单或运单) evidencing dispatch from a mainland customs port to a Taiwan port
Inward Remittance Certificate (出口收汇核销/银行收汇水单) with SWIFT or cross-strait RMB clearing details matching the LC/TT payment rail
Commercial Invoice and Detailed Packing List (商业发票及装箱单)
VAT Special E-Invoice for export sales (出口发票/数电票) and input VAT special invoices (进项增值税专用发票) reconciling the rebate calculation
Production Enterprise Export Goods Exemption-Credit-Refund Declaration Form (生产企业出口货物免抵退税申报表)
GACC food export inspection release / health certificate (出境货物检验检疫通关单/兽医卫生证书) for steamed dim sum
Export Contract with the Taiwan buyer (出口合同) specifying Incoterms and settlement terms
Original or verified copy of processing records confirming the self-production nature of the exported goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SAT, GACC, and SAFE jointly operate the Golden Tax Phase IV matching engine that verifies export declarations, B/L data, foreign exchange receipts, and refund claims in real time. Fraudulent zero-rating (false customs declarations, fake B/Ls, over-invoicing, matched-pair round-tripping between mainland and Taiwan entities, or unrepatriated proceeds) triggers: (1) retrospective clawback of all VAT refunds with statutory late-payment interest at 0.05% per day; (2) an administrative penalty of 50%–500% of the reclaimed tax under the Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63; (3) a specific export-tax-fraud penalty of 1–5 times the defrauded amount; (4) criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Article 204 with imprisonment from 5 years to life for aggravated fraud; (5) revocation of VAT general taxpayer status and export rebate qualification with a minimum 3-year disqualification period; (6) inclusion in the joint disciplinary blacklist (失信名单) affecting customs clearance, banking, and cross-border settlement facilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China maintains current account convertibility for trade in goods and services, including profit remittances from a WFOE, which are processed by designated banks upon verification of audited financial statements, tax clearance, and the foreign exchange registration record. Capital account transactions remain subject to prior SAFE registration/approval, mandatory foreign exchange reporting, and negative-list restrictions on foreign investment. Profit remittance is permitted through the current account category, but requires documentary proof of distributable reserves and withholding tax settlement; no mandatory conversion of RMB profits is imposed, yet capital-account FX conversion must strictly adhere to the approved business scope and use-purpose verification under SAFE Circular 19 and subsequent rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China has eliminated mandatory surrender of export proceeds since 2012. Export receipts in foreign currency must be repatriated to mainland China through a designated foreign exchange bank and either retained in the enterprise's foreign currency settlement account or converted into RMB at the enterprise's discretion. SAFE's trade verification system enforces a statutory collection timeline generally set at 180 days from the export customs declaration date for general trade, unless an extension is obtained from SAFE. For a frozen dim sum processing WFOE, export receipts must be matched with the China International Trade Single Window declarations and supplier invoices; no fixed mandatory conversion ratio applies to current account receipts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI and payment institutions are not licensed to open corporate accounts or provide proprietary clearing infrastructure within mainland China. A WFOE cannot lawfully rely on an offshore EMI as its primary treasury or settlement rail. Cross-border fund movements must flow through Chinese licensed banks or approved non-bank cross-border payment institutions acting as processors, with underlying trade or investment documentation available to SAFE and the bank. Offshore EMIs may support ancillary foreign currency receipts only by clearing via a corresponding Chinese bank account, which does not replace the need for a domestic corporate banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for initial corporate account opening by a mainland China WFOE. The legal representative, or an authorized senior officer with a notarized power of attorney, must appear in person at the chosen bank branch for a face-to-face KYC interview and transaction-activity explanation. Remote onboarding is not universally permitted for new foreign-invested enterprises; some banks allow video-based interviews only as a supplement after the physical branch visit. Non-resident directors who do not hold a mainland residence permit may issue a notarized and legalized power of attorney to a local officer, but the ultimate beneficial owners still must satisfy the bank's UBO identification procedure before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership chain involving a Taiwan intermediate investment vehicle and layered shareholding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate chain chart with registry extracts from Taiwan and mainland China; UBO declaration forms per mainland AML rules; certified copies of business registration and investment approval; board resolutions; audited financial statements of the shareholder; source-of-funds declaration supported by bank statements and sale/purchase agreements for the invested capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection expected from a Taiwan entity whose main business is not clearly linked to food manufacturing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply and co-manufacturing agreement between the WFOE and the Taiwan shareholder; food production license (SC license / food production permit) of the mainland factory; build-operate-transfer or equipment purchase contracts; customs declaration records for raw material imports; projected cash flow model of the dim sum production line; bank reference letter from the Taiwan shareholder's bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume related-party cross-border payments without clear commercial substance or order history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany services or goods supply agreements reflecting arm's-length pricing; transfer pricing documentation or comparable analysis; detailed demand forecasts and purchase orders for quick-frozen steamed dim sum ingredients; board-approved treasury management policy; historical shipping and customs records; bank statements showing consistent operational cash flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or director identified as a politically exposed person (PEP).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP and adverse-media screening report; source of wealth and source of funds documentation for the PEP; certified passport and proof of residential address; notarized declaration of legitimate business purpose; enhanced due diligence report from a licensed compliance advisory firm; audited financial statements of the PEP's corporate interests; legal opinion confirming no unlawful political contribution or influence-peddling structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound FDI capital from the Taiwan shareholder must be remitted through a designated bank in mainland China to the WFOE's foreign exchange capital account (FDI Capital Account) using the SAFE-approved remittance purpose code for foreign direct investment (generally 'Direct investment – Capital injection' / code 622011 or the relevant prevailing SAFE code set). Prior to remittance, the WFOE must complete the foreign investment information report with the Ministry of Commerce/SAMR and obtain the SAFE FX registration via the bank (via the FX Capital Account Registration system). The remitter must be the registered foreign shareholder; third-party remittance is not permitted unless the bank verifies a genuine chain of funds and SAFE reporting. After funds are received, RMB conversion is permitted only for approved uses such as purchase of production equipment, raw materials for dim sum manufacturing, wages, rent, utilities, and other operating expenses within the WFOE's registered business scope. The bank will monitor the use of the converted RMB funds under the negative-list regime and may require filing of capital account use declarations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements from the mainland WFOE to Taiwan suppliers or service providers must clear through SWIFT MT103 wires or documentary trade instruments. For raw ingredient imports (e.g., frozen seafood fillings, flour, seasonings), the preferred rail is SWIFT MT103 with payment purpose code reflecting general trade settlement, reconciled against the China International Trade Single Window electronic customs declaration, commercial invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, and packing list. For larger equipment purchases or long-dated supply contracts, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (sight L/C) issued by the WFOE's mainland bank in favor of the Taiwan beneficiary is recommended; settlement occurs against presentation of compliant shipping documents. All outward remittances must be matched to the underlying transaction in the bank's trade verification system (e.g., 货贸外汇收支申报), with applicable withholding tax certificates if service imports are involved. Payments to Taiwan may be subject to additional documentary scrutiny under SAFE's cross-border payment consistency verification, especially when the payee is a related party.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB foreign exchange forwards (plain vanilla, trade-backed, tenors generally up to 12 months) permitted under SAFE real-demand verification

Onshore RMB cross-currency swaps (fixed-floating or fixed-fixed) executed with a licensed Chinese bank for hedging underlying trade or investment cash flows, subject to business genuineness documentation

CFTC/ISDA-documented non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) available to the offshore Taiwan-side counterparty only; mainland WFOE is restricted from direct offshore NDF participation, but may indirectly hedge through the Taiwan parent treasury using back-to-back onshore forwards

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval no later than 30 June (within 6 months of the 31 December fiscal year end); filing with MOEA within 15 days of shareholder approval, generally by 15 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning and per-violation fines of TWD 20,000–200,000 for late filing; continued non-compliance permits MOEA to order correction and may culminate in compulsory dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May following the close of the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warning, suspension of review of foreign-investment applications, or order to rectify; repeated non-filing may impair the legal status of the foreign investment approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May through 31 May following the close of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of TWD 3,000, plus interest and a 2% surcharge on unpaid tax for each two-week installment; intentional non-filing may result in a penalty of up to twice the underpaid tax and criminal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of TWD 1,000–15,000 for late or inaccurate filing; under-withheld amounts subjected to arrears interest and additional tax penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan limited company, including a WFOE, is required to have annual financial statements audited by a licensed CPA if it is a public company, a financial enterprise, or a non-public company with paid-in capital of at least TWD 30 million or annual net revenue of at least TWD 100 million; MOEA may also require audits for designated industries
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Profit-seeking enterprises apply the Business Entity Accounting Act and related regulations; public companies and large non-public companies apply Taiwan-IFRS as endorsed by the FSC; small non-public companies may apply ROC GAAP, which is substantially converged with IFRS for major recognition and measurement principles

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation return. Under Company Act Article 22-1, a non-public company must update and file the register of material controllers with MOEA within 15 days of any change in shareholding or control. Foreign investors must also provide current beneficial-ownership details in the annual Investment Commission operations report. A written UBO register must be maintained at the registered office and made available for inspection by competent authorities.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – 1,500 per year for corporate secretarial and registered-office services by a local CPA/agent firm
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – 8,000 per year for a mid-sized frozen-food processing WFOE requiring a statutory CPA audit and tax coordination

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax on the taxable income of a Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible enterprises may access sector-specific investment tax credits, accelerated depreciation, research and development credits, selected smart machinery or green-energy incentives, and approved investment incentives under Taiwan investment legislation. Dividends received by a Taiwan company from another Taiwan company may generally qualify for an intercompany dividend deduction, subject to statutory conditions. No general corporate income tax holiday applies to an ordinary frozen-food processing company solely because it is foreign-owned. Qualifying losses may be carried forward for up to 10 years where statutory bookkeeping, blue-return, and filing conditions are satisfied; the mandatory schema value of 5 years is not the general Taiwan statutory period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Taiwan Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書), including applicable schedules for taxable income, tax adjustments, related-party transactions, withholding, fixed assets, inventory, and retained earnings; electronic filing through the National Taxation Bureau e-filing system operated by the Ministry of Finance (財政部電子申報繳稅服務網).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; monthly or bimonthly business tax returns and periodic withholding tax returns are separate obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For an enterprise using a calendar fiscal year, the annual settlement return and final corporate income tax payment are generally due from 1 May through 31 May following the end of the tax year. An enterprise using an approved non-calendar fiscal year generally files within the fifth month after fiscal year-end. Extensions require specific statutory or administrative authorization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the unified business number, legal name, registered address, fiscal year, accounting currency, tax agent information, filing type, and whether the return is an amended, late, liquidation, or dissolution return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan subsidiary or branch files under its Taiwan tax identification number. The foreign parent is not substituted for the Taiwan taxpayer. A non-resident enterprise with Taiwan-source income normally uses withholding or other prescribed source-tax procedures unless it has a Taiwan permanent establishment or fixed place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report profit or loss before Taiwan tax based on audited or properly maintained financial statements, with reconciliation to tax accounting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-parent income that is not attributable to Taiwan activities. Allocate Taiwan-attributable income and expenses using consistent books and defensible functional analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible or limited deductions, including unsupported expenses, excess depreciation, disallowed entertainment, penalties, non-business expenses, insufficiently documented related-party charges, and expenses failing withholding requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to the foreign parent require contracts, invoices, benefit evidence, withholding analysis, transfer-pricing support, and proof of remittance where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Revenue and exempt or separately taxed income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify domestic sales, export sales, service income, interest, dividends, capital gains, subsidies, and other income according to Taiwan tax treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export revenue may remain subject to Taiwan corporate income tax because the income is earned by the Taiwan entity. VAT treatment and corporate income tax treatment must be analyzed separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cost of goods sold and inventory
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile opening inventory, purchases, direct labor, manufacturing overhead, closing inventory, production yield, wastage, obsolescence, and inventory valuation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For imported ingredients, packaging, machinery, or services from the foreign parent, retain customs records, import declarations, intercompany invoices, and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax depreciation using approved useful lives and methods; reconcile book depreciation, tax depreciation, disposals, construction in progress, and capitalized interest where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party asset transfers require arm's-length valuation, customs and import documentation, and analysis of withholding, VAT, stamp tax, and corporate income tax consequences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report salaries, bonuses, employer contributions, expatriate compensation, benefits, and employee-related taxes and insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-parent secondees require employment, recharge, permanent-establishment, individual withholding, social insurance, and benefit-in-kind analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Interest, royalties, technical fees, and service charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify deductible financing costs and cross-border charges, apply statutory withholding where required, and reconcile related-party amounts with the transfer-pricing report.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not treat a payment as a deductible business expense merely because it is invoiced by the foreign parent. Establish actual services, commercial benefit, cost allocation, arm's-length pricing, and treaty eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter approved prior-year losses used against current taxable income and maintain schedules showing origin, expiry, utilization, and remaining balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward generally requires timely filing, proper books, and compliance with Taiwan statutory conditions. Ownership changes, business cessation, reorganizations, and non-compliant bookkeeping may restrict utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and corporate income tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate taxable income after statutory adjustments, apply the 20% rate, deduct allowable credits and prepayments, and determine the final balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require qualifying foreign tax, supporting certificates, income attribution, and compliance with statutory limitation rules. Foreign tax cannot be deducted and credited for the same income where prohibited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determine whether Taiwan alternative minimum tax applies because of specified exempt income, securities transactions, overseas income, or other add-back items under the Income Basic Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan company with foreign-source income or incentive-based deductions must test alternative minimum tax separately from ordinary corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose related parties, transaction categories, amounts, jurisdictions, financing, royalties, services, purchases, sales, and transfer-pricing methods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with the foreign parent and affiliates even where no adjustment is proposed. Reconcile tax-return disclosures to audited accounts, customs data, withholding returns, and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the additional tax applicable to undistributed earnings generated in the relevant year, subject to statutory deductions and qualifying reinvestment rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan company should model the additional tax before declaring dividends, funding capital expenditures, or making qualifying reinvestments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit the electronic return, payment confirmation, accountant or tax-agent certification where required, financial statements, transfer-pricing documents, and prescribed schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Electronic submission does not eliminate record-retention duties. Keep source documents, customs records, contracts, board approvals, payment evidence, and tax certificates for the statutory retention period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger a surcharge generally calculated by reference to tax payable, commonly 10% of the assessed tax subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts. Failure to file may trigger a higher surcharge, commonly 20% of tax payable subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts. Interest accrues on unpaid tax from the statutory payment deadline. Inaccurate returns may result in additional tax, penalties, denial of deductions, and criminal referral where intentional evasion is established. Separate penalties may apply for failure to file withholding, business tax, or information returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% withholding tax generally applies to dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a non-resident shareholder. The domestic rate may be reduced under an applicable Taiwan income tax agreement or other statutory relief, subject to eligibility and beneficial-ownership requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, confirm that the recipient is the beneficial owner, verify the applicable income-tax agreement and limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse conditions, collect ownership and substance evidence, and apply the reduced rate only where Taiwan procedures permit relief at source. Where advance approval, ruling, or refund application is required, submit the prescribed application to the competent National Taxation Bureau before or after payment as applicable. Retain the certificate, agreement analysis, shareholder register, board resolution, payment record, and withholding filing. A Taiwan-China cross-strait arrangement must not be assumed to operate as an ordinary bilateral income-tax treaty; the payment jurisdiction, recipient residence, and applicable cross-strait rules require separate confirmation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic withholding rate is generally 20% on Taiwan-source interest paid to a non-resident and 20% on Taiwan-source royalties or similar remuneration for the use of intellectual property. An applicable income-tax agreement may reduce the rate, subject to treaty definitions, beneficial ownership, residence certification, anti-avoidance rules, and any required advance approval. Technical services, software, know-how, equipment rentals, guarantee fees, and mixed service arrangements require characterization analysis because different withholding rules may apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan generally requires a Local File for qualifying cross-border controlled transactions unless an applicable exemption applies, including the threshold under which total annual controlled transactions are below approximately TWD 200 million, subject to transaction-specific rules. A Master File is generally required for a Taiwan enterprise meeting the large-enterprise criteria, commonly including annual net operating revenue of at least TWD 3 billion or aggregate cross-border controlled transactions of at least TWD 1 billion, subject to the current regulations and prescribed exemptions. A Country-by-Country Report may apply to a Taiwan constituent entity of a multinational enterprise group meeting the applicable consolidated-revenue threshold, generally EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a single standalone OECD-style Economic Substance Regulation regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless relevant under Taiwan transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership analysis, the general anti-avoidance rule, controlled foreign company rules, permanent-establishment principles, treaty anti-abuse standards, and business-purpose doctrines. The Taiwan entity should maintain real employees, premises, production assets, decision-making, inventory control, quality systems, procurement functions, risks, and commercial activity proportionate to its claimed manufacturing profile. A low-risk manufacturer with no personnel, no production control, or no operational capacity may face recharacterization, deduction denial, transfer-pricing adjustment, withholding exposure, or permanent-establishment concerns.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating purchases, understating inventory, creating false invoices, diverting company revenue, claiming fictitious related-party expenses, or intentionally submitting materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax, statutory surcharge, interest, assessment of omitted income, and potential criminal liability under Taiwan tax laws. Intentional evasion can result in imprisonment and criminal fines; the applicable sentence depends on the offense, amount, evidence, and judicial findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, responsible persons, managers, accountants, and other participants may incur criminal liability where they personally direct, approve, assist, or conceal the conduct. Civil restitution, tax recovery, asset preservation, disqualification consequences, and potential travel restrictions may arise in enforcement proceedings. Piercing of limited liability is not automatic and generally requires personal wrongdoing, fraud, abuse of corporate form, or statutory grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing and fraudulent expense deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-genuine uniform invoices, circular trading, sham procurement, inflated raw-material purchases, fabricated service fees, or backdated contracts to reduce taxable income or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of deductions and input tax credits, additional tax, penalties, interest, invoice-related sanctions, and possible criminal prosecution for false documentation, tax evasion, or fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons who authorize or knowingly use false documents may face personal criminal prosecution, civil tax restitution, director or officer liability, and seizure or freezing of assets. Imprisonment is fact-dependent and may apply where the conduct satisfies the relevant criminal offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting manufacturing profit through excessive royalties, management fees, procurement mark-ups, interest, guarantee fees, underpriced exports, or unsupported cost allocations to the foreign parent or affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taiwan tax authorities may make an arm's-length adjustment, deny deductions, impose additional corporate income tax, assess withholding tax, charge interest, and apply documentation or reporting penalties. Corresponding adjustments are not automatic.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed where they knowingly approve non-arm's-length arrangements, false documentation, or deliberate profit diversion. Ordinary disagreement over method selection generally does not create personal criminal liability absent fraud, concealment, or intentional evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, services, rentals, commissions, or other Taiwan-source amounts to a foreign recipient without withholding, withholding at an unsupported treaty rate, or failing to remit and report withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Taiwan payer may be assessed the unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, surcharges, filing penalties, and possible liability for failure to collect or remit tax. The payer generally cannot cure the exposure merely by asserting that the foreign recipient was contractually responsible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons and withholding agents may incur administrative and criminal exposure for deliberate failure to withhold or remit. Directors may face personal claims where they authorized the payment and tax diversion or acted fraudulently.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign parent conducts Taiwan sales, contract negotiation, procurement, manufacturing supervision, or other core activities through the Taiwan company or personnel while reporting only routine manufacturing income or no Taiwan-source profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Attribution of additional Taiwan-source income, corporate income tax, withholding tax, penalties, interest, and possible reassessment of intercompany charges. Treaty protection may be denied where the facts satisfy a permanent-establishment or dependent-agent test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and administrative exposure for knowingly maintaining inaccurate functional descriptions or tax returns. Criminal liability generally requires intentional concealment, fraud, or evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and insufficient economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Taiwan company that has no genuine employees, premises, production capability, inventory responsibility, management decisions, or commercial risks while routing invoices or profits through the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of deductions, reallocation of income, treaty-benefit denial, withholding assessments, transfer-pricing adjustments, VAT reassessment, and potential fraud or tax-evasion prosecution where records are fictitious.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil restitution, asset tracing, injunctions, and criminal liability if the entity is used to conceal ownership, launder funds, evade tax, or issue false documents. Limited liability does not protect intentional personal misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering and suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unexplained third-party funds, structuring payments, using nominee accounts, processing circular transfers, disguising shareholder loans, or making payments inconsistent with the food-manufacturing business profile.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction suspension or rejection, suspicious transaction reporting, account restrictions, administrative penalties, confiscation, and criminal sanctions under Taiwan anti-money-laundering and criminal laws where money laundering or predicate offenses are established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, compliance officers, and employees may be personally liable for knowing participation, assistance, concealment, or willful blindness. Criminal penalties may include imprisonment, fines, asset confiscation, and restrictions on financial activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating frozen-food processing without required registration or permits, using unsafe ingredients, falsifying labels, breaching cold-chain requirements, or exporting products without required sanitary and customs documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Product seizure, recall, destruction, production suspension, license cancellation, administrative fines, business closure, civil claims, and criminal prosecution for serious food-safety violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face personal administrative and criminal liability where they knowingly approve unsafe production, conceal contamination, falsify records, or obstruct inspection. Civil compensation may include consumer and commercial losses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying ingredients or machinery, undervaluing imports, falsifying country of origin, manipulating customs valuation, or using intercompany pricing to evade customs duties and import taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional customs duty, import tax, VAT, penalties, seizure, forfeiture, loss of customs privileges, and possible criminal prosecution for smuggling or fraudulent declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and customs declarants may face personal liability where they knowingly submit false declarations or participate in duty evasion. Asset seizure and criminal restrictions may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized capital withdrawal or disguised profit distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repaying shareholder loans without substance, transferring assets below value, paying excessive related-party charges, distributing dividends without distributable earnings, or using company funds for foreign-owner personal expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, deemed dividend withholding, corporate law sanctions, restoration of company assets, shareholder repayment obligations, civil damages, and possible criminal liability for breach of trust or misappropriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may be required to restore funds, compensate the company or creditors, and face criminal prosecution for breach of fiduciary duty, embezzlement, fraud, or unlawful distribution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain books and records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain Mandarin or legally acceptable accounting records, destruction of source documents, inconsistent ledgers, unsupported cash transactions, or refusal to provide records during a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Bookkeeping penalties, estimated assessment, denial of deductions, loss carryforward denial, additional tax, interest, and enhanced scrutiny of all related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may face personal sanctions where record destruction or obstruction is intentional. Criminal exposure increases when poor records conceal tax evasion, money laundering, or false invoicing.
